guides.theme: A Jeskai Marvel Heroes typal deck: Captain America rewards each Hero entering with +1/+1 counters and gives the team haste and vigilance, while the dense legendary Hero roster, tribal payoffs, and counter/equipment support build an aggressive go-wide Avengers team. Director Nick Fury is the included alternate commander, emphasizing cheaper Hero spells and a steady stream of Heroes.

picks.name: Envoy of the Ancestors
picks.reason: The EDHREC guide's budget package recommends it because Captain America's counters make its team-wide keyword support especially valuable.
picks.budgetNote: The opened EDHREC guide explicitly labels this among its Five Additions on a Budget; no numeric price is asserted.

picks.name: Honor-Worn Shaku
picks.reason: The guide recommends this additional mana rock; the deck's high legendary count lets it produce substantial mana.
picks.budgetNote: The opened EDHREC guide explicitly labels this among its Five Additions on a Budget; no numeric price is asserted.

picks.name: Scholar of New Horizons
picks.reason: The guide recommends it as a way to keep land development on pace by converting a +1/+1 counter into a basic-land search.
picks.budgetNote: The opened EDHREC guide explicitly labels this among its Five Additions on a Budget; no numeric price is asserted.

picks.name: Wave Goodbye
picks.reason: The guide recommends it as a one-sided-friendly reset that leaves the counter-enhanced Avengers board ready to attack.
picks.budgetNote: The opened EDHREC guide explicitly labels this among its Five Additions on a Budget; no numeric price is asserted.

alternatePaths.title: Director Nick Fury Hero-cost reduction
alternatePaths.description: Use the included alternate commander to reduce the cost of Hero spells and generate extra Heroes in hand, shifting from Captain America's enter-the-battlefield counter/haste plan toward sustained Hero deployment and resource flow.
alternatePaths.linkLabel: EDHREC Director Nick Fury precon page

swaps.rationale: Curated like-for-like creature slot: replace a creature the guide says is better in a deck built around its own ability with a budget Hero-support creature that capitalizes on Captain America's counters.
Curated creature-to-ramp conversion: the guide recommends cutting Wasp's defensive role in favor of proactive spells, and Honor-Worn Shaku leverages the deck's legendary Heroes for mana.
Curated creature-to-mana-development conversion: the guide identifies Patriot as a cuttable protection creature and recommends Scholar to turn excess counters into land access.

Curated noncreature swap: the guide specifically recommends cutting Hero's Blade for a more synergistic effect; Wave Goodbye preserves an aggressive, board-based plan by clearing blockers while keeping the Avengers board largely intact.

guides.theme: Grixis Villains built around Doctor Doom's combat connive: discard excess lands to drain opponents, grow or enable Villain payoffs, and use menace/evasion and token-making to attack. Loki is the more aggressive alternate leader, rewarding connecting with multiple Villains. The deck also has a secondary discard/draw and exile/suspend package around Molecule Man, Kang Prime, and Doom's Time Platform.

picks.name: Leader, Super-Genius
picks.reason: A native Marvel Villain that rewards the deck's repeated connive and discard triggers; EDHREC lists it as the most common add, and the budget guide pairs it with M.O.D.O.K.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was provided; the budget guide presents it as a core low-cost-style upgrade without quoting a price.

picks.name: M.O.D.O.K.
picks.reason: Supports the same connive engine as Leader, turning life payments into extra draw/discard while remaining an on-theme Villain; explicitly recommended by the budget guide and listed by EDHREC.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was provided; the budget guide recommends it but gives no dollar figure.

picks.name: Doom Reigns Supreme
picks.reason: A flavor-perfect upgrade that adds another Doom plan while reinforcing the deck's Villain, connive, and cosmic-domination identity; EDHREC ranks it highly and the budget guide calls it an auto-include.
picks.budgetNote: The guide describes it as budget-friendly but provides no source price.

picks.name: Construct a Cosmic Cube
picks.reason: Keeps the deck's Doom-specific plan and provides an on-theme payoff for its Villain/connive shell; the budget guide calls it an auto-include and EDHREC lists it as a common add.
picks.budgetNote: The guide describes it as budget-friendly but provides no source price.

picks.name: Compulsion
picks.reason: The budget guide specifically recommends it as inexpensive recursive draw: it triggers Molecule Man on opponents' turns while also feeding Doom's discard synergies.
picks.budgetNote: The source explicitly calls Compulsion inexpensive, but gives no numeric price.

alternatePaths.title: Loki-led aggressive Villains
alternatePaths.description: Use Loki, the Deceiver as commander for a more restrictive but combat-forward Villain build: connect with each opponent to draw more cards and prioritize Villains worth copying or having twice.

alternatePaths.title: Molecule Man discard-and-draw engine
alternatePaths.description: Keep Doctor Doom at the helm but pivot the 99 toward repeated draw triggers: inexpensive recursive-draw cards such as Compulsion, Trade Routes, and Tectonic Reformation make Molecule Man cast the first card drawn each turn for free and feed Doom's discard plan.

swaps.rationale: Curated like-for-like Villain value swap: Leader directly rewards the deck's connive pattern, while Helmut is among EDHREC's most-cut cards.
Curated Villain-for-Villain swap that moves from a narrower Treasure/life-loss role to a stronger connive payoff explicitly supported by the upgrade guide.
Curated plan-for-plan swap: the guide identifies the precon's Glorious Purpose as the existing plan and recommends Doom Reigns Supreme as the stronger Doom-specific plan.
Curated on-theme enchantment swap: both are named Marvel schemes/payoffs, but the guide specifically recommends the Cosmic Cube while EDHREC shows Age of Ultron as a frequent cut.
Curated creature swap: Archfiend is an EDHREC-supported discard payoff that converts the deck's connive/discard into board control; Titania is a frequent EDHREC cut.
Curated Villain creature swap using EDHREC's add and cut rankings; it preserves the Marvel Villain identity while upgrading the creature slot.
Curated Villain-for-Villain swap: Green Goblin is a frequent EDHREC add and Batroc a frequent cut, preserving the deck's native Marvel world and typal plan.
Curated Villain creature swap supported by EDHREC add/cut rankings; both occupy the combat-oriented Marvel Villain role.
Curated Marvel Villain upgrade supported by EDHREC's add/cut rankings; it keeps the deck in-universe while replacing a commonly removed creature.
Curated engine swap: the budget guide recommends Compulsion as inexpensive recursive draw for Molecule Man and Doom, while naming Damocles Base among its cuts.

Curated engine swap: Trade Routes repeatedly picks up and discards lands for Molecule Man and Doom, while Endless Ranks of HYDRA is an EDHREC-supported cut and appears in the guide's broader cut package.
Curated draw/discard-engine swap: Tectonic Reformation is recommended for recurring discard triggers and Syphon Mind is a frequent EDHREC cut.

Curated interaction/tutor swap: the budget guide recommends Muddle as both cheap interaction and a transmute tutor for the new engine, while Extract Power is a frequent EDHREC cut and is listed in the guide's cuts.
Curated tutor/evasion swap: the budget guide recommends Ethereal Usher to find Molecule Man or Lady Loki's Manifestation and enable unblockable attacks; Lady Loki is a frequent EDHREC cut.

guides.theme: A four-color Marvel Fantastic Four deck built around casting noncreature spells—especially rebound and flashback spells—then getting beginning-of-combat payoffs, copied triggered abilities, card draw, and combat pressure. Mister Fantastic is the most natural stock-build commander; Invisible Woman leans into token generation and unblockable damage, while Human Torch and The Thing are more focused Voltron paths.

picks.name: Venture Forth
picks.reason: Budget upgrade from the EDHREC guide that adds another noncreature ramp spell, helping the four-color deck reach its expensive spells and fix mana.
picks.budgetNote: The guide labels this a budget addition but does not provide a current price; no price is asserted here.

picks.name: Primeval Bounty
picks.reason: The EDHREC guide's budget list includes this durable noncreature payoff, giving the deck value when it continues casting spells and developing creatures.
picks.budgetNote: The guide labels this a budget addition but does not provide a current price; no price is asserted here.

picks.name: Faithful Mending
picks.reason: A budget noncreature spell that smooths draws and has flashback, directly supporting the deck's cast-a-spell and recurring-spell plan.
picks.budgetNote: The guide labels this a budget addition but does not provide a current price; no price is asserted here.

picks.name: Nature's Lore
picks.reason: EDHREC lists it among frequent adds; cheap land ramp is especially useful for a four-color deck whose plan depends on casting large noncreature spells.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC provides an add ranking but no source price in the opened page; no price is asserted here.

picks.name: Beast Within
picks.reason: EDHREC lists it among frequent adds; flexible noncreature interaction preserves the deck's central spell-payoff engine while answering any permanent.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC provides an add ranking but no source price in the opened page; no price is asserted here.

alternatePaths.title: Invisible Woman token-and-evasion plan
alternatePaths.description: Use Invisible Woman as the commander, add more token makers, and turn a growing board into unblockable combat damage; the EDHREC guide specifically identifies token effects as the way to make her ability consistently lethal.

alternatePaths.title: The Thing counters/Voltron plan
alternatePaths.description: Use The Thing as commander and shift the list toward +1/+1 counters and combat; the EDHREC guide describes him as a Voltron option that amasses counters and doubles counters across the board.

swaps.rationale: Curated like-for-like ramp swap: the upgrade article calls Fellwar Stone reliable fixing and says The Fantasticar lacks enough cheap noncreature enablers in this list.
Curated draw upgrade: the article favors Hex Magic's explosive ceiling over giving opponents cards with Cut a Deal.
Curated noncreature-payoff swap: the article says Capstone supports the noncreature theme and combat-step triggers, while Nova Flame is less synergistic here.
Curated creature swap: the article says Silver Surfer does not mesh with the deck, while Monica's Photon side applies pressure; both names are individually supported by the opened sources.
Curated sweeper swap: the article supports a mostly one-sided tribal-style wipe because the deck's creatures are largely heroes, replacing a broader reset.
Curated value swap: the upgrade article recommends Restoration Seminar as a stronger fit for recurring the deck's spell-centric value than Genesis Ultimatum.
Curated ramp swap: both are noncreature ramp effects, while the EDHREC guide specifically praises Venture Forth as a budget addition and calls Terramorph slow.
Curated spell-smoothing swap: Faithful Mending keeps the flashback/recurring-spell identity while filtering earlier and costs less up front than Deep Analysis.
Curated consistency swap: EDHREC lists Nature's Lore as a frequent add and Willie Lumpkin as a frequent cut; land ramp better supports the color-intensive spell plan.
Curated interaction-for-outlier swap: EDHREC supports Beast Within as an add and Galactus as a frequent cut; flexible removal advances the noncreature-spell plan more reliably.
Curated interaction swap: EDHREC supports Counterspell as an add and Black Bolt as a cut; a cheap noncreature answer is more consistently useful in the deck's spell chain.
Curated removal swap: EDHREC supports Swords to Plowshares as an add and Ultimate Nullification as a cut; efficient creature removal improves the noncreature interaction suite.
Curated protection-for-flexibility swap: EDHREC supports Heroic Intervention as an add and Collective Effort as a cut, protecting the board while keeping the deck's spell count high.
Curated cheap-interaction swap: EDHREC supports Arcane Denial as an add and Promise of Loyalty as a cut; the lower-cost counterspell better enables chaining noncreature spells.

guides.theme: A green-white Wakandan artifacts deck: T'Challa turns combat into extra Vibranium mana rocks, which pay for expensive artifacts, equipment, activated abilities, and mana sinks. The native subthemes are artifact creatures, Equipment/Voltron, +1/+1 counters, and monarch/diplomacy; Shuri offers the more aggressive artifact-creature/diplomacy route.

picks.name: Dyadrine, Synthesis Amalgam
picks.reason: The EDHREC guide's budget package specifically recommends this large artifact payoff to exploit free Vibranium while staying on the deck's artifact plan.
picks.budgetNote: Listed by EDHREC under its budget additions; no numeric price was provided in the opened source.

picks.name: Valor's Flagship
picks.reason: A budget-package artifact payoff that makes the deck's surplus Vibranium mana matter and preserves the Wakandan artifact identity.
picks.budgetNote: Listed by EDHREC under its budget additions; no numeric price was provided in the opened source.

picks.name: Yotian Dissident
picks.reason: The guide recommends it as a value engine for the many free Vibranium tokens, adding a native +1/+1-counter payoff.
picks.budgetNote: Listed by EDHREC under its budget additions; no numeric price was provided in the opened source.

picks.name: Digsite Engineer
picks.reason: A budget-recommended mana sink that converts the deck's extra mana into artifact creature bodies.
picks.budgetNote: Listed by EDHREC under its budget additions; no numeric price was provided in the opened source.

picks.name: Steel Hellkite
picks.reason: The guide's budget package uses this artifact mana sink as scalable removal and a threat, directly leveraging Vibranium acceleration.
picks.budgetNote: Listed by EDHREC under its budget additions; no numeric price was provided in the opened source.

alternatePaths.title: Shuri-led aggressive diplomacy
alternatePaths.description: Swap T'Challa for Shuri, the Black Panther when you want the deck's artifact subtheme to attack more aggressively and apply pressure with artifact creatures; the official decklist and EDHREC guide both identify Shuri as the alternate commander.

alternatePaths.title: T'Challa artifact Voltron/counters
alternatePaths.description: Keep T'Challa in the command zone but emphasize Equipment, Voltron, and +1/+1 counters around the Vibranium engine; these are the leading EDHREC tags for T'Challa and retain the precon's native mechanics.

swaps.rationale: Curated like-for-theme swap: replace the guide's identified low-synergy token enchantment with its budget-recommended large artifact payoff.
Curated artifact-for-artifact replacement: Flagship is a proactive Vibranium-powered mana sink, while EDHREC notes the Cloak's shroud prevents equipping more gear to T'Challa.
Curated creature-for-creature replacement: Dissident turns the deck's recurring Vibranium tokens into counters, while the guide calls T'Chaka an unnecessary monarch-recovery slot.
Curated creature-for-creature replacement: Engineer converts spare mana into artifact bodies, replacing the guide's cut candidate that mainly recovers monarch.
Curated payoff replacement: Hellkite is a repeatable artifact mana sink/removal threat, whereas EDHREC says Visitation has little support because few cards make creature tokens.

Curated artifact-creature replacement: Ironsoul is a high-lift EDHREC artifact recommendation and keeps the deck focused on artifact recursion/value rather than an under-supported token-doubling effect.
Curated artifact-for-artifact value swap: Forge is a high-lift EDHREC artifact recommendation that rewards the deck's unusually high artifact density.
Curated creature-for-creature swap: Familiar is an EDHREC high-lift artifact support card that discounts the deck's many historic spells, unlike the guide's weaker monarch-recovery creature.
Curated artifact-for-artifact swap: Guardian supplies artifact-count scaling and team protection, while the guide flags Cloak's shroud as awkward for an equipment-heavy T'Challa plan.
Curated creature-for-creature swap: Karn is an EDHREC high-lift artifact mana payoff that fits T'Challa's surplus-mana plan better than the guide's monarch-recovery cut candidate.

alternatePaths.title: Excava, the Risen Past recursion build
alternatePaths.description: Use Excava as commander for an attack-driven recursion plan: return a low-mana artifact, creature, or non-Aura enchantment from the graveyard as a flying Spirit with a finality counter. EDHREC presents Excava as the alternate commander and notes that a deck built specifically for it can make the plan shine.

guides.theme: A five-color kindred-on-kindred party deck: Morophon discounts and buffs a chosen creature type while changelings/Shapeshifters count as every type. picks.name: Changeling Outcast

guides.theme: A Jeskai (blue-red-white) spellslinger deck built around casting multiple noncreature spells each turn. Shiko and Narset reward the second spell each turn, especially when it targets a permanent or player; the deck uses cheap cantrips, magecraft/prowess-style payoffs, cost reduction, and copied or replayed instants and sorceries. Elsha is the featured alternate commander and shifts emphasis toward aggressive prowess and Monk-token combat.

picks.name: Dig Through Time
picks.reason: A low-cost delve draw/filter spell that turns the spent graveyard of cantrips and interaction into two of the best seven cards, directly supporting the deck's high-spell-count plan.
picks.budgetNote: The opened sources recommend it but do not quote a current price; verify the market price before buying.

picks.name: Increasing Vengeance
picks.reason: A cheap instant that copies an instant or sorcery and has flashback, giving Shiko and Narset more targetable spell-copy value while remaining on-theme.
picks.budgetNote: No price was quoted by the opened sources; treat this as a budget candidate, not a guaranteed price claim.

picks.name: Press the Enemy

picks.name: Coruscation Mage

alternatePaths.title: Elsha prowess-and-Monk tokens
alternatePaths.description: Use Elsha, Threefold Master as commander and keep the spellslinger shell, but prioritize casting many noncreature spells in explosive turns, connecting in combat, and multiplying Monk tokens. EDHREC suggests more damage/evasion, token production, and better Monk payoffs; this is a real strategic shift rather than a generic commander swap.

picks.budgetNote: Included in EDHREC's budget upgrade list; no source price was stated.

picks.name: Dispatch
picks.reason: Cheap artifact-synergy interaction that EDHREC specifically adds to improve the precon's removal package while Clues help enable metalcraft.
picks.budgetNote: Included in EDHREC's budget upgrade list; no source price was stated.

picks.name: Swiftfoot Boots
picks.reason: Protects Morska or another key payoff, preserving the creature-and-token plan; EDHREC includes it in the budget upgrade list.
picks.budgetNote: Included in EDHREC's budget upgrade list; no source price was stated.

picks.name: Yotian Dissident
picks.reason: Turns every artifact entering the battlefield—including Clues and other token artifacts—into +1/+1-counter progress, multiplying Morska's native counter plan.
picks.budgetNote: Included in EDHREC's budget upgrade list and add rankings; no source price was stated.

alternatePaths.title: Sophia-led Dog/Food/Clue build
alternatePaths.description: Use the included Sophia, Dogged Detective as commander for a narrower line centered on her legendary Dog, Food and Clue generation from combat, and artifact-token payments for Dog counters. EDHREC identifies Sophia as the backup commander and describes this play pattern.

alternatePaths.title: Morska counter-win line
alternatePaths.description: Keep Morska at the helm but emphasize second-card draws, +1/+1 counters, Hardened Scales, and Simic Ascendancy; EDHREC's guide presents Ascendancy as an additional win condition for the counter-heavy upgrade.
alternatePaths.linkLabel: EDHREC Deep Clue Sea Upgrade Guide

swaps.rationale: Curated like-for-like token swap. EDHREC explicitly makes this replacement because Avenger produces more tokens that can grow; Hornet Queen is confirmed in the original list.
Curated Clue-engine swap: a repeatable Investigate/venture payoff replaces a low-impact artifact. Ransom Note is in the precon, and both EDHREC's add and cut data support the direction.
Curated interaction swap: efficient artifact-enabled removal for a costly counterspell whose three Clues do not compensate for its five-mana rate in this slot.
Curated utility swap: protect the commander and key engines instead of relying on a slow, mana-intensive Clue-making rock; both cards' add/cut support appears in EDHREC coverage.
Curated counter-synergy swap: Dissident rewards every artifact entering and advances Morska's counter plan; Serene Sleuth is one of the precon cards most often cut on EDHREC.
Curated artifact-value swap: Steelseeker turns artifact entries into card selection, matching the Clue/token engine; Innocuous Researcher is an EDHREC-supported cut candidate.
Curated counter payoff swap: Hardened Scales amplifies Morska and the deck's other counter sources, while Armed with Proof is a documented EDHREC cut candidate.
Curated artifact-token finisher swap: Rise and Shine converts the deck's accumulated Clues and other artifacts into a creature army, while Killer Service is an EDHREC-supported cut.
Curated alternate-win swap: Ascendancy rewards the counter-heavy Morska plan and is explicitly presented by EDHREC as another way to win; Nadir Kraken is an EDHREC-supported cut candidate.

Curated land-function swap: EDHREC's guide recommends Rogue's Passage to push Morska through, while EDHREC's precon data flags Temple of the False God as a frequent cut; both are validated against the original list.

guides.theme: Dimir surveil-and-reanimation: fill the graveyard through repeatable Surveil, grow Mirko with +1/+1 counters, then recur creatures and exploit enter-the-battlefield and death-value effects. The deck is from Murders at Karlov Manor (MKC); Mirko is the primary commander and Marvo is the second new-to-Magic commander.

picks.name: Snarling Gorehound
picks.reason: Budget repeatable Surveil outlet; small-creature entries, including Mirko and many reanimated bodies, keep the graveyard engine moving.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC's upgrade article places it in the budget (about $5 or less) section; no current price asserted.

picks.name: Sanguine Spy
picks.reason: Low-cost repeatable Surveil that turns expendable creatures into selection, especially useful with Mirko's recursion.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC's article places it in the budget section; no current price asserted.

picks.name: Wayfarer's Bauble
picks.reason: Addresses the precon's stated low ramp count without leaving the graveyard/reanimation plan.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC's article places it in the budget section; no current price asserted.

picks.name: Power Conduit
picks.reason: Moves counters off creatures carrying Finality counters and converts Mirko's +1/+1-counter plan into protection against permanent exile-from-graveyard effects.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC's article places it in the budget section; no current price asserted.

picks.name: Corpse Connoisseur
picks.reason: Entombs the best reanimation target on entry and repeats that job when reanimated, directly reinforcing the deck's core loop.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC's article includes it in the budget upgrade; no current price asserted.

alternatePaths.title: Marvo, Deep Operative: alternate Dimir commander
alternatePaths.description: Use the precon's second commander as the lead instead of Mirko; EDHREC lists Marvo as the principal alternate on the deck page, while the upgrade article explicitly removes Marvo from its Mirko build.

alternatePaths.title: Lazav, the Multifarious: graveyard-copy path
alternatePaths.description: A supported alternate commander listed by EDHREC for this precon; it keeps the Dimir graveyard creature pool but shifts emphasis toward copying creatures in the graveyard rather than Mirko's counter-based reanimation trigger.

swaps.rationale: Curated ramp upgrade: Bauble is the article's budget ramp addition; Chalice is an official precon mana-rock cut named by the article.
Curated value-for-ramp swap: Hart is an article-supported budget ramp/reanimation target; Ransom Note is an official precon card named among the article's cuts.
Curated creature-slot swap: Simulacrum adds ramp and is a strong Mirko resurrection target; Phantasm is an official precon card named as a cut.
Curated like-for-like Surveil creature swap: Gorehound supplies repeatable Surveil from the article's budget recommendations; Spybug is a named precon cut.
Curated creature-slot swap toward repeatable Surveil and sacrifice value; both sides are individually supported by the article and official list.
Curated Surveil-density swap: Witness turns the deck's many noncreature spells into repeatable Surveil; Curate is a precon card and a named cut.
Curated counter-management swap: Conduit directly answers Finality counters and supports Mirko's counters; Zenith is an article-supported cut from the official list.
Curated interaction swap: Heartless Act handles creatures and can remove counters; Dispersal is a named official-precon cut.
Curated protection-for-flexible-spell swap: the article adds Boots to protect Mirko; Counterpoint is an official precon card named among the cuts.
Curated draw/value swap: Ayara rewards the deck's recurring black creatures and may draw cards; Arena is an article-supported cut.
Curated finisher-for-selection swap: Gray Merchant converts the deck's black board presence into a reanimation-friendly life swing; Discovery // Dispersal is a named cut.

Curated setup-for-top-end swap: instant-speed Entomb loads the exact reanimation target; Dream Eater is a named article cut and official precon card.

guides.theme: A Naya (red-green-white) go-wide tribal-token deck built around Cats, Dogs, and Rin and Seri's ability to make the other creature type while dealing damage. It also uses creature-type payoffs, token anthems, and a small number of broader token engines; the official product includes three display commander options.

picks.name: Beast Within
picks.reason: Flexible instant-speed removal that addresses any permanent and fills the precon's documented shortage of varied instant-speed interaction.
picks.budgetNote: No price was quoted in the opened sources; treat as a budget-conscious utility candidate and verify current price before buying.

picks.name: Shared Animosity
picks.reason: A native go-wide combat payoff: Cats, Dogs, and the tokens Rin and Seri create turn a wide board into a much faster attack.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was available; this is a theme-preserving upgrade rather than a claimed price quote.

picks.name: Idol of Oblivion
picks.reason: Repeatable card draw for a deck that reliably creates tokens, improving the precon's engine without changing its Cat/Dog plan.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was quoted; verify current market price and use a cheaper printing if needed.

picks.name: Warleader's Call
picks.reason: An anthem that also rewards the deck's creature-token production, giving the native swarm plan both pressure and incidental damage.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was available; select only if its current price fits the budget.

picks.name: Grand Crescendo
picks.reason: Instant-speed protection that also makes Soldiers, preserving a go-wide board against wipes while adding bodies for Rin and Seri payoffs.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was quoted; verify current price rather than assuming a dollar amount.

alternatePaths.title: Jetmir go-wide anthem plan
alternatePaths.description: Use Jetmir, Nexus of Revels as commander and lean harder into the deck's broad creature-token board; both EDHREC's commander navigation and Wizards' official product page identify Jetmir as a deck commander/display commander.

alternatePaths.title: Jinnie Fay token-conversion plan
alternatePaths.description: Use Jinnie Fay, Jetmir's Second and convert token creation into efficient Cat or Dog bodies, retaining the deck's animal-token identity while changing the token-engine emphasis.

swaps.rationale: Curated like-for-like removal upgrade: instant-speed, any-permanent interaction replaces a slower enchantment-based answer.

Curated Dog-synergy creature upgrade: Tesak supplies counters and haste support for the animal swarm.
Curated go-wide combat upgrade: Mirri makes a token attack harder to block and limits the crackback.
Curated creature-slot swap toward token payoff and board resilience rather than conditional land finding.
Curated instant-speed protection/token-maker replacement for a high-variance reset that the article specifically dislikes in this deck.
Curated protection-for-mana-rock/clone swap to address the precon's limited response package and protect a developed board.
Curated finisher swap: immediate protection/evasion and team-wide power are more aligned with the deck's go-wide close than a six-mana top-end enchantment.
Curated board-protection upgrade that protects the full token army instead of only providing a narrow personal shield.

guides.theme: Grixis Pirate tribal combat: mill Pirates into the graveyard, recur one as a hasty 4/4 with Admiral Brass, and convert evasive attacks into cards, Treasure, theft and extra combats. The native Lost Caverns of Ixalan identity is Pirates, graveyard recursion/Finality counters, Treasure and combat pressure.

picks.name: Breeches, Eager Pillager
picks.reason: A Pirate that rewards attacking with Treasure, impulse-played cards and a temporary power boost; it directly increases the deck's combat-and-Treasure engine.
picks.budgetNote: Named in the EDHREC budget upgrade guide; no source price was supplied, so verify the current price before buying.

picks.name: Forerunner of the Coalition
picks.reason: A Pirate tutor that finds a key Pirate and drains opponents when Pirates attack, improving both consistency and the go-wide combat plan.
picks.budgetNote: Included by the EDHREC budget upgrade guide; no source price was supplied, so verify the current price.

picks.name: Power Conduit
picks.reason: Provides instant-speed removal of Finality counters, allowing Brass's reanimated Pirates to survive a later death while converting unused counters into +1/+1 counters.
picks.budgetNote: Specifically presented as a budget counter-removal upgrade; no source price was supplied.

picks.name: Nesting Grounds
picks.reason: A low-opportunity-cost land that can move Finality counters off Brass's returned creatures during the main phase, supporting the deck's recursion loop.
picks.budgetNote: Specifically recommended by the EDHREC budget guide; no source price was supplied.

picks.name: Dire Fleet Neckbreaker
picks.reason: A Pirate anthem that gives attacking Pirates a substantial power boost, preserving the precon's native go-wide combat plan.
picks.budgetNote: Included in the EDHREC budget upgrade list; no source price was supplied.

alternatePaths.title: Admiral Beckett Brass theft build
alternatePaths.description: Use the precon's other Pirate commander to lean harder into connecting with three Pirates and permanently stealing opponents' creatures; EDHREC exposes a dedicated Ahoy Mateys upgrade page for this commander.
alternatePaths.linkLabel: EDHREC Admiral Beckett Brass Ahoy Mateys page

alternatePaths.title: Don Andres larceny package
alternatePaths.description: Keep Don Andres as commander and expand the small theft package (Threaten-style effects, stolen permanents and spells) instead of focusing purely on Brass's graveyard recursion; the EDHREC review identifies this as the deck's alternate theft direction.

swaps.rationale: Curated like-for-like Pirate creature swap: a combat/Treasure engine replaces a slower opponent-draw body; both candidates are individually supported by EDHREC.
Curated Pirate-for-Pirate swap that trades a narrow evasion body for tribal tutoring and attack drain.
Curated evasive-Pirate swap: both support connecting in combat, while the suggested Malcolm adds card selection and Treasure.
Curated Pirate utility swap: targeted disruption and evasion support replaces a narrower recursion creature.
Curated Pirate-for-Pirate swap that turns the deck's Treasure production into a scaling board threat.
Curated tribal-draw upgrade: a repeatable Pirate draw engine replaces a one-shot creature-count draw spell.
Curated synergy swap: copying Pirates and their enter-the-battlefield effects is more native to Brass's recursion plan than the narrow theft aura.
Curated Pirate payoff swap: discard-triggered damage and cycling support the deck's draw/attack engine without the Ravager's life-total drawback.
Curated combat-finisher swap: a Pirate anthem improves the whole attacking team rather than equipping one creature.
Curated interaction swap: blink protects and reuses a Pirate's enter-the-battlefield value while preserving the board, unlike a symmetrical mass bounce.
Curated graveyard setup swap: filling the graveyard with selected Pirates directly enables Admiral Brass, while the cut is a slower reactive payoff.
Curated protection swap: cheap unconditional stack interaction protects the recursion engine more efficiently than a four-mana removal spell.
Curated tribal-enchantment swap: repeated combat damage draw better matches the deck's evasive Pirate plan than a creature-selection anthem.
Curated Treasure payoff swap: the deck already contains substantial Treasure generation, so a thematic payoff can replace a low-impact late-game ramp card.
Curated artifact utility swap: counter removal protects Brass's reanimated Pirates and directly addresses the precon's Finality-counter gap.

guides.theme: Orzhov Vampire aristocrats: attack with Vampires, sacrifice blessed Vampires to create 4/3 Vampire Demon tokens, and convert creature deaths into life drain, counters, cards, and recursion. The native Lost Caverns of Ixalan identity is Vampire tribal plus sacrifice/death-trigger payoffs, with Clavileño as the primary build-around.

picks.name: Acolyte of Aclazotz
picks.reason: Adds a repeatable sacrifice outlet and life-drain payoff, directly reinforcing Clavileño's blessed-Vampire death plan.
picks.budgetNote: The EDHREC article places it in the budget upgrade section; no source price was supplied.

picks.name: Bloodmist Infiltrator
picks.reason: Provides an attack-triggered sacrifice outlet while helping Vampires connect for damage.
picks.budgetNote: The EDHREC article places it in the budget upgrade section; no source price was supplied.

picks.name: Relic Vial
picks.reason: A Cleric-synergy sacrifice outlet that turns sacrificed creatures into card advantage and life loss.
picks.budgetNote: The EDHREC article recommends it in the early budget-upgrade package; no source price was supplied.

picks.name: Bastion of Remembrance
picks.reason: Adds a token body and a dependable death-trigger life-drain engine for the aristocrats shell.
picks.budgetNote: The EDHREC article includes it among the budget upgrades; no source price was supplied.

picks.name: Tenured Inkcaster
picks.reason: Converts the deck's Vampire-token production into repeatable life loss and +1/+1 counters.
picks.budgetNote: The EDHREC article includes it among the budget upgrades; no source price was supplied.

alternatePaths.title: Carmen, Cruel Skymarcher sacrifice/value
alternatePaths.description: Use Carmen as the commander for a more sacrifice-centric Orzhov Vampire/aristocrats build; EDHREC lists Carmen as an alternate commander on the Blood Rites precon page and discusses Carmen's multiple triggered abilities in the upgrade guide.

alternatePaths.title: Elenda, the Dusk Rose token/death snowball
alternatePaths.description: Shift toward Elenda's death-trigger token engine while retaining the precon's Vampire aristocrats core; EDHREC lists Elenda as an alternate commander for this exact precon.
alternatePaths.linkLabel: EDHREC Blood Rites upgrades for Elenda, the Dusk Rose

guides.theme: A Naya Dinosaur tribal deck led by Pantlaza, Sun-Favored. It ramps into large Dinosaurs, then uses the first Dinosaur entering each turn to Discover from the top of the library; the native shell also supports Dinosaur ETB/enrage-style value, combat pressure, and token production.

picks.name: Fellwar Stone
picks.reason: Cheap, broadly useful ramp that helps the deck cast its high-mana Dinosaurs sooner; explicitly recommended as a budget ramp upgrade.
picks.budgetNote: The opened EDHREC article calls it a budget upgrade but gives no price; verify the current price before buying.

picks.name: Nature's Lore
picks.reason: Low-cost land ramp that improves early development without changing the Dinosaur/Discover plan.
picks.budgetNote: The opened EDHREC article calls it a budget upgrade but gives no price; verify the current price before buying.

picks.name: Kodama's Reach
picks.reason: Reliable two-land ramp that supports the precon's expensive threats and is explicitly included in EDHREC's budget package.
picks.budgetNote: The opened EDHREC article calls it a budget upgrade but gives no price; verify the current price before buying.

picks.name: Lightning Greaves
picks.reason: Protects Pantlaza or a key Dinosaur while granting haste, directly addressing the article's concern that the commander needs protection.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC describes it as near the budget/non-budget boundary but gives no price; verify the current price before buying.

picks.name: Gishath, Sun's Avatar
picks.reason: A high-impact Dinosaur that the EDHREC guide says is absent from the base deck and adds it as a premier Dinosaur payoff; it also preserves the deck's native tribe and can be an alternate commander.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was quoted; verify the current price before buying.

alternatePaths.title: Gishath Dinosaur beatdown
alternatePaths.description: Keep the same Naya Dinosaur shell but move Gishath, Sun's Avatar to the command zone for a more combat-focused Dinosaur plan; the opened guide calls Gishath the likely best Dinosaur commander and recommends considering it.

alternatePaths.title: Atla Palani top-deck creature engine
alternatePaths.description: A more creature-cheat-oriented route using Atla Palani, Nest Tender; the EDHREC upgrade guide specifically describes Reinforcements as especially strong with a commander that plays creatures from the top of the deck, such as Atla, while retaining the Dinosaur shell.

Curated protection-for-threat swap: the guide recommends Heroic Intervention to defend the board and cuts Earthshaker Dreadmaw.
Curated protection-for-threat swap: the guide recommends Teferi's Protection as board-wide defense and cuts Quartzwood Crasher.

guides.theme: A Bant Doctor Who historic-spells deck: cast artifacts, Sagas, and legendary spells to exploit Doctor/legend synergies, create Food and Clue artifacts, recur or copy historic permanents, and potentially assemble the Gallifrey Stands alternate win condition with 13 Doctors. The native set/world theme is Doctor Who, with a secondary legends-and-token package.

picks.name: Raff Capashen, Ship's Mage
picks.reason: EDHREC recommends it, and the upgrade article specifically uses Raff to give historic spells flash so Gallifrey Stands and the needed Doctors can be deployed at the right moment.
picks.budgetNote: No price claim made; verify current market price before purchase.

picks.name: Sally Sparrow
picks.reason: A Doctor Who-native addition supported by both EDHREC and the article; it helps cast the Doctors needed for the Gallifrey Stands plan.
picks.budgetNote: No price claim made; verify current market price before purchase.

picks.name: The Eleventh Doctor
picks.reason: EDHREC recommends it and the article identifies it as one of the two additional Doctors that fit this deck's color identity, directly advancing the 13-Doctor plan.
picks.budgetNote: No price claim made; verify current market price before purchase.

picks.name: Clara Oswald
picks.reason: The article adds Clara to double Doctor triggers, while EDHREC lists her as an upgrade; she preserves the deck's Doctor and historic focus.

picks.name: Everybody Lives!
picks.reason: EDHREC recommends it and the article uses it as protection for the Doctor board needed for Gallifrey Stands; it is a focused defensive upgrade rather than an off-theme staple.

guides.theme: Azorius flying aggro with a Sphinx top end, anthem effects, token-making, and a secondary incentives-for-being-attacked/control package. The native plan is to build a wide evasive board, amplify fliers, draw from combat or attacks, and use efficient interaction to keep the skies clear.

picks.name: Crib Swap
picks.reason: Theme-preserving instant-speed creature removal that leaves an opposing Changeling body behind, giving Isperia a plausible future attack trigger while answering a key threat.
picks.budgetNote: The upgrade article states that none of its recommended additions costs more than $10; it does not give an individual current price.

picks.name: Pongify
picks.reason: One-mana creature removal that gives the opponent a relatively small ground body; the token can be blocked by the deck's fliers and still supports Isperia's attack-trigger draw plan.
picks.budgetNote: The upgrade article states that none of its recommended additions costs more than $10; it does not give an individual current price.

picks.name: Rapid Hybridization
picks.reason: A second one-mana creature answer with the same give-them-a-ground-body pattern, improving interaction without diluting the flying plan.
picks.budgetNote: The upgrade article states that none of its recommended additions costs more than $10; it does not give an individual current price.

picks.name: Watcher of the Spheres
picks.reason: A cheap flying creature that reduces the cost of later fliers and grows with the deck's native flying-creature count, accelerating the core mechanic.
picks.budgetNote: The upgrade article presents it as an imperative flying-tribal addition but gives no individual price; do not infer a price.

picks.name: Court of Grace
picks.reason: Creates flying tokens and makes the pilot Monarch, reinforcing both the deck's evasive board and its native incentive-for-opponents-to-attack-you subtheme.
picks.budgetNote: The upgrade article gives no individual price; no price is asserted here.

alternatePaths.title: Dragonlord Ojutai flying aggro
alternatePaths.description: Replace Isperia with Dragonlord Ojutai and keep the wide fliers shell, shifting from opponent-controlled attack-trigger draw to a cheaper, more controllable commander with hexproof while untapped; add vigilance/protection support.
alternatePaths.linkLabel: EDHREC First Flight Precon Upgrade Guide

alternatePaths.title: Sphinx tribal
alternatePaths.description: Lean harder into the deck's existing Sphinx concentration, using the smaller flying creatures and cost reducers as support for a higher-impact Sphinx top end; the cited guide explicitly identifies this as a viable alternate theme.

guides.theme: A blue-black Zombie graveyard toolbox: self-mill and discard stock the graveyard, then Gisa and Geralf let you cast a Zombie from it each turn. The build emphasizes high-quality enters-the-battlefield and death triggers, recursion, sacrifice outlets, and repeatable removal rather than going wide with tokens.

picks.name: Undead Butler
picks.reason: Self-mills and has an enters-the-battlefield/death-value profile that directly supports the article's Zombie toolbox plan.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was provided; selected as a compact utility creature rather than a premium staple.

picks.name: Crow of Dark Tidings
picks.reason: Adds repeatable graveyard filling through its ETB/death triggers and is explicitly recommended for the deck's reanimation plan.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was provided; chosen as a low-complexity graveyard enabler that preserves the native Zombie theme.

picks.name: Forgotten Creation
picks.reason: Provides recurring hand filtering, effectively a repeatable Windfall to put Zombies and recursion targets in the graveyard.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was provided; selected for inexpensive-looking role compression, not a claimed price.

picks.name: Secrets of the Dead
picks.reason: Turns Gisa and Geralf's graveyard casting into card advantage whenever a Zombie is cast from the graveyard.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was provided; a focused engine piece is preferred over a broad, expensive staple.

picks.name: Carrion Feeder
picks.reason: A free sacrifice outlet that enables death-trigger loops and grows while keeping the deck's Zombie identity.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was provided; selected as a simple, theme-native sacrifice outlet.

guides.theme: A Gruul modified-matters deck: Chishiro rewards Auras and Equipment by making 2/2 Spirit tokens and rewards modified creatures with +1/+1 counters. The native plan is to keep creatures modified, build a wide board of Spirits, and finish through combat/Voltron pressure. The EDHREC upgrade article specifically recommends shifting the precon toward cheap, recurring Auras and enchantress-like value while retaining the token-and-counters plan.

picks.name: Rancor
picks.reason: A cheap Aura that repeatedly returns when it goes to the graveyard, giving Chishiro another modified trigger while adding trample to a countered attacker; it is the EDHREC page's most-added card.
picks.budgetNote: No itemized price was stated in the opened sources; selected as the top EDHREC add and a low-complexity Aura fit.

picks.name: Renata, Called to the Hunt
picks.reason: Adds a +1/+1 counter to each new creature and reinforces the deck's modified-creature and Spirit-token plan; it is a high-ranked EDHREC add and is explicitly recommended by the budget guide.
picks.budgetNote: The opened budget guide presents Renata in its $50 upgrade; it does not quote a current card price.

picks.name: Hardened Scales
picks.reason: Improves every +1/+1-counter placement, amplifying Chishiro's counter engine and other native counter cards; it is one of the EDHREC page's leading adds.
picks.budgetNote: No price was quoted in the opened sources; selected from the EDHREC add rankings for direct theme fit.

picks.name: Inspiring Call
picks.reason: Protects a counter-heavy board from a destroy effect while drawing cards, directly supporting the deck's modified-creature payoff plan; it is an EDHREC add and is explicitly recommended by the budget guide.
picks.budgetNote: The opened budget guide includes Inspiring Call in its budget upgrade but gives no current price.

picks.name: Wild Growth
picks.reason: A one-mana Aura that ramps while triggering Chishiro's Aura-based token engine; the EDHREC page lists it as an add and the budget guide explicitly recommends it for ramp.
picks.budgetNote: The opened budget guide names Wild Growth as part of its $50 upgrade but does not quote a current price.

alternatePaths.title: Aura-focused Chishiro
alternatePaths.description: Keep Chishiro as commander but replace a substantial portion of the less efficient Equipment and creatures with cheap, recurring Auras plus enchantress-like card advantage. This preserves Spirits, modified creatures, and Voltron pressure while increasing Aura-trigger consistency.

alternatePaths.description: The Card Kingdom guide identifies Uril, the Miststalker as a Gruul Voltron alternative: use the precon's Aura shell to build one hard-to-interact-with lethal creature rather than emphasizing Chishiro's token-wide plan.

guides.theme: Golgari Elf tribal: deploy Lathril early, connect with menace to make Elf Warrior tokens, then go wide, tap the team for Lathril's activated ability, or win through Elf lords and life-drain effects. guides.theme: A five-color Dragon tribal battlecruiser deck: The Ur-Dragon's eminence reduces Dragon costs, while attacks draw cards and put permanents onto the battlefield. guides.theme: Bant combat and board-control precon built around Derevi's tap/untap triggers, with a secondary blink/enter-the-battlefield (ETB) package inherited from Roon of the Hidden Realm. guides.theme: Four-color combat aggression: Saskia makes damage to one opponent echo to another, while the precon goes wide with tokens and small creatures, then converts attacks into lethal pressure through haste, evasion, combat buffs, and damage amplification. The original list also contains a secondary partner package around Tana, the Bloodsower with Tymna the Weaver or Ravos, Soultender.

picks.name: Cultivate
picks.reason: Adds reliable two-land ramp and color fixing while keeping the deck's creature-combat plan intact; EDHREC lists it among the most common additions and the upgrade article places it in its <$5 suggestions.
picks.budgetNote: The article groups this under its <$5 upgrade recommendations; no current price is asserted.

picks.name: Kodama's Reach
picks.reason: A second inexpensive basic-land ramp/fixing effect that helps cast a four-color commander and is explicitly recommended by both opened upgrade sources.
picks.budgetNote: The article groups this under its <$5 upgrade recommendations; no current price is asserted.

picks.name: Champion of Lambholt
picks.reason: Turns the precon's go-wide creature plan into scalable attack evasion; EDHREC ranks it as a common add and the article calls it a good Saskia evasion option.
picks.budgetNote: The article includes it in its <$5 suggestions; no current price is asserted.

picks.name: Rhythm of the Wild
picks.reason: Provides haste or a +1/+1 counter to new creatures, directly reinforcing the deck's aggressive creature-and-token curve; EDHREC lists it as an add.
picks.budgetNote: No source price is available here, so no price is claimed.

picks.name: Dictate of the Twin Gods
picks.reason: Doubles combat damage and pairs naturally with Saskia's additional damage trigger; both EDHREC and the budget article support it as a damage-amplification add.
picks.budgetNote: The article includes it in its <$5 suggestions; no current price is asserted.

alternatePaths.title: Saskia infect conversion
alternatePaths.description: The opened upgrade article explicitly presents infect as an alternate Saskia direction: use high-power infect threats or grant infect to a creature, then combine evasion and damage doublers to end games quickly. This is a major strategy shift rather than a native precon upgrade.

swaps.rationale: Curated like-for-like ramp upgrade: Cultivate gives dependable land-based fixing instead of relying on opponents' creature counts.
Curated like-for-like ramp/fixing swap that improves color reliability without changing the combat plan.
Curated combat-evasion swap: Champion scales with a go-wide board and helps attackers connect, while Wilderness Elemental is less consistently threatening here.
Curated enchantment-for-enchantment swap: Rhythm gives immediate haste or counters without handing an opponent a matching counter engine.
Curated damage-enchantment swap: Dictate directly multiplies Saskia combat output, whereas Torment is mainly a prevention/lifegain-hosing effect.
Curated removal upgrade: efficient unconditional creature exile is more reliable than a conditional threaten-and-sacrifice line.
Curated aggression swap: Battledriver turns every new creature or token into immediate pressure, matching the precon's go-wide plan.
Curated combat-enchantment swap: double strike boosts Saskia's damage plan and can be offered politically, while Fugue is a temporary control effect.
Curated creature-support swap: Uprising supplies trample and ongoing card draw for large attackers, while Hermit is a slower token package.
Curated finisher-for-graveyard-enchantment swap: Triumph converts a wide board into a lethal attack, preserving the deck's aggressive identity.
Curated top-end damage-engine swap: Gisela multiplies the deck's combat and Saskia damage, while Mycoloth asks for an upkeep investment before producing value.
Curated extra-combat swap: Aurelia gives a repeatable attack trigger without requiring the fragile creature-enchantment connection that Breath of Fury needs.
Curated protection-for-high-variance-spell swap: Intervention protects the established board and commander, preserving the deck's combat setup.
Curated flexible-removal swap: Unmaking answers any problematic nonland permanent instead of waiting for a high-land-count damage spell.
Curated recursion upgrade: Sun Titan repeatedly returns small permanents and creatures, broadening the precon's attrition plan beyond Den Protector's one-shot recursion.

guides.theme: Orzhov enchantment-matters: cast enchantments to build Daxos's experience counters, then turn them into scalable Spirit tokens; the stock list also contains a secondary lifegain/Karlov package, but enchantments and recursion are the native core.

picks.name: Grim Guardian
picks.reason: Turns each enchantment entering the battlefield into an opponent life-loss trigger, directly rewarding the deck's enchantment density.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC lists it as an add; no individual price was supplied by the opened sources, so no price is asserted.

picks.name: Starfield Mystic
picks.reason: Reduces the cost of the deck's many enchantments and grows when enchantments go to the graveyard, improving both tempo and late-game scaling.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC lists it as an add; no individual price was supplied by the opened sources, so no price is asserted.

picks.name: Archon of Sun's Grace
picks.reason: Makes lifelinking Pegasus tokens whenever an enchantment enters, adding a second token engine beside Daxos's Spirits.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC lists it as an add and the EDHREC upgrade article includes it in its budget remaster; the article gives a deck total, not an individual card price.

picks.name: Skybind
picks.reason: Uses constellation triggers to blink permanents, enabling repeatable value from enchantment ETBs and protecting or reusing key pieces.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC lists it as an add and the opened upgrade article recommends it; no individual price was supplied.

picks.name: Gift of Immortality
picks.reason: Protects an important creature and returns to hand after the delayed return trigger, preserving the recursive enchantment play pattern.
picks.budgetNote: EDHREC lists it as an add and the opened upgrade article recommends it; no individual price was supplied.

alternatePaths.title: Karlov of the Ghost Council lifegain
alternatePaths.description: Move the commander slot to Karlov and emphasize the precon's incidental lifegain, using enchantments such as Underworld Coinsmith, Phyrexian Arena, and Underworld Connections as support. This is a distinct secondary path explicitly identified by the upgrade coverage.
alternatePaths.linkLabel: Two Directions For Commander 2015's Call The Spirits Deck

alternatePaths.title: Daxos enchantments-matter
alternatePaths.description: Keep Daxos as commander and focus tightly on enchantment casting, experience-counter accumulation, recursive enchantments, and token production. The cited coverage describes this as the obvious/native direction for Call the Spirits.

swaps.rationale: A stronger enchantment-based defense replaces a mana-intensive creature ability; both sources support the candidate directions.
Converts every enchantment into pressure and is more aligned with Daxos's main plan than the lifegain subtheme.
Improves enchantment casting and scaling rather than relying on a slower, off-plan token combat body.
Adds a repeatable enchantment-triggered token engine in place of a costly generic attacker.
Improves the many Spirit and other token attacks with vigilance and a team-wide power boost.
Provides a more reliable enchantment-based answer to a threatening commander or creature.
Trades a narrow aura for scalable enchantment-based combat protection.
Adds a durable enchantment with life-drain and enters-tapped utility instead of a low-impact aura.
Keeps a creature returning and the aura reusable, supporting the article's recursive enchantment engine.
A board reset that is specifically listed for the enchantment build and better preserves an enchantment-heavy battlefield.
Creates more tokens and grants vigilance, reinforcing the deck's primary battlefield plan.
Upgrades creature removal while retaining the enchantment type and instant-speed interaction.
Exchanges a slow, scalable spell for efficient creature interaction; both candidates are directly listed by EDHREC.
Adds graveyard hate on an enchantment-supporting creature and removes a creature the article identifies as not belonging in the plan.
Replaces a conditional refill body with recursion for many of the deck's low-cost permanents.
Turns Daxos and other token production into a stronger board-wide payoff.
Adds an enchantment-count payoff and more Spirits, while removing a low-synergy aura creature.
Doubles Daxos and other token makers instead of adding another narrow land-search creature.
Reclaims an enchantment and supports the deck's recursion loop; both appear in the opened EDHREC upgrade coverage.
Keeps the bestow/enchantment-creature role while scaling from the deck's enchantment and creature count.
Reduces enchantment costs and directly advances the enchantment-matters plan.

guides.theme: Golgari graveyard recursion and sacrifice: fill the graveyard, sacrifice creatures for value, build Meren experience counters, then repeatedly return creatures and win through death triggers, token production, or a large overrun-style finish.

picks.name: Spore Frog
picks.reason: A repeatable sacrifice-and-recur fog that directly rewards Meren's experience-counter and graveyard loop plan; it is the EDHREC precon's top card addition.
picks.budgetNote: No individual price was supplied by the opened sources; verify current market price before buying.

picks.name: Fleshbag Marauder
picks.reason: A cheap, repeatable edict body: sacrifice it, force opposing sacrifices, and recur it with Meren; it is explicitly highlighted by the EDHREC article and ranked highly as an add.
picks.budgetNote: No individual price was supplied by the opened sources; verify current market price before buying.

picks.name: Reclamation Sage
picks.reason: Adds a creature-based artifact/enchantment answer that can be reused through Meren; EDHREC lists it among common additions.
picks.budgetNote: No individual price was supplied by the opened sources; verify current market price before buying.

picks.name: Blood Artist
picks.reason: Turns the deck's steady sacrifice and recursion into life loss and life gain, reinforcing the native death-trigger plan; included in the EDHREC remastered build and add rankings.
picks.budgetNote: No individual price was supplied by the opened sources; verify current market price before buying.

picks.name: Viscera Seer
picks.reason: A low-cost free sacrifice outlet that scries while enabling Meren experience counters and death-trigger loops; it is an EDHREC-supported add.
picks.budgetNote: No individual price was supplied by the opened sources; verify current market price before buying.

alternatePaths.title: Jarad, Golgari Lich Lord sacrifice finisher
alternatePaths.description: Switch the commander to Jarad for a more direct sacrifice-and-graveyard damage plan, using the same large-creature recursion shell.

alternatePaths.title: Mazirek, Kraul Death Priest counters-and-sacrifice path
alternatePaths.description: Shift the focus from Meren experience counters toward mass +1/+1 counters whenever permanents are sacrificed; the EDHREC article specifically uses Mazirek with sacrificed myriad tokens as the synergy example.

swaps.rationale: Curated like-for-like creature sacrifice upgrade: Spore Frog provides a repeatable defensive sacrifice loop, while Banshee is the EDHREC-cut leader.
Curated sacrifice/reanimation improvement: Fleshbag is a cheap edict body that the article recommends, whereas Champion's five-mana activation is criticized in the article.
Curated creature-based permanent-removal swap: both answer artifacts/enchantments, but the lower-cost Sage is a more efficient recursion target.
Curated death-trigger payoff for a less focused top-end creature; Dictate is an EDHREC-supported add and turns every sacrifice into table-wide pressure.
Curated low-curve utility swap: Caterpillar is a sacrificeable, recur-able answer and an EDHREC-supported add; Caller is among the frequent cuts.
Curated interaction swap: Plaguecrafter supplies a recur-able edict, while the article calls Cloudthresher a weak big beater and suggests cheaper flyer interaction.
Curated value swap: Blood Artist converts the deck's repeated deaths into a win condition, while Rager is a less synergistic one-shot card-draw body.
Curated sacrifice-outlet upgrade: Ashnod's Altar provides repeatable mana from deaths, while Blood Bairn is one of EDHREC's most common cuts.
Curated low-cost engine swap: the free outlet enables scry, death triggers, and Meren experience loops more reliably than the expensive mill creature.
Curated finisher swap: Cutthroat rewards every sacrifice immediately; Verdant Force is a slower token engine and an EDHREC-supported cut candidate.
Curated scalable death-and-recur finisher: Gray Merchant converts a developed black board into a life swing, while Thief is a frequent EDHREC cut.
Curated card-advantage swap: Haruspex draws as creatures die and is easier to reuse incrementally than the higher-cost Augur.
Curated theme-first draw upgrade: Reclamation turns the deck's normal sacrifice pattern into repeatable draw and life gain rather than a one-shot spell.
Curated recursion swap: the EDHREC article says Journey to Eternity is easy to flip in this shell and criticizes Diabolic Servitude's reanimation performance.
Curated mass-recursion finisher: the EDHREC article explicitly prefers Living Death over the deck's weaker reanimation package and Rise from the Grave is an original card being replaced.

guides.theme: Izzet spellslinger/control: cast a high density of instants and sorceries to build Mizzix's experience counters, reduce later spell costs, and finish with scalable X-spells, copied/recurred spells, and value engines. The stock list also contains a secondary wheel/draw-seven angle through Arjun, Jace's Archivist, Dragon Mage, and related draw effects.

picks.name: Guttersnipe
picks.reason: Turns the deck's core instant-and-sorcery plan into repeatable table damage and is the most frequently added creature on the Mizzix precon page.
picks.budgetNote: Listed in the opened MTGGoldfish $20 upgrade pool; no individual price was stated in the source, so no price is claimed here.

picks.name: Tezzeret's Gambit
picks.reason: Provides card draw while proliferating Mizzix's experience counters, directly reinforcing the commander engine.
picks.budgetNote: Included in the opened MTGGoldfish $20 upgrade pool; the source gives no individual price.

picks.name: Frantic Search
picks.reason: Cheap instant-speed filtering that untaps lands, helping the deck chain spells and exploit Mizzix cost reductions.
picks.budgetNote: Included in the opened MTGGoldfish $20 upgrade pool; the source gives no individual price.

picks.name: Ponder
picks.reason: A low-cost cantrip that improves spell density and card selection while building experience counters early.
picks.budgetNote: Included in the opened MTGGoldfish $20 upgrade pool; the source gives no individual price.

picks.name: Counterspell
picks.reason: Efficient protection for Mizzix and a clean upgrade to the deck's control posture; it appears among EDHREC's adds and the article's disruption pool.
picks.budgetNote: Included in the opened MTGGoldfish $20 upgrade pool; the source gives no individual price.

alternatePaths.title: Melek copy/spellslinger path
alternatePaths.description: Use Melek, Izzet Paragon as the commander for a more explosive top-of-library spell-copying plan. The opened article directly compares Melek with Mizzix, while EDHREC lists Melek as a Seize Control commander option.
alternatePaths.linkLabel: EDHREC Seize Control upgrades for Melek, Izzet Paragon

alternatePaths.title: Arjun wheel/draw-seven path
alternatePaths.description: Keep the precon's wheel subtheme and center the build on Arjun, the Shifting Flame, Jace's Archivist, and Dragon Mage to repeatedly replace hands while retaining the Izzet spell package. The opened upgrade article identifies this as a subtheme and names Arjun as an alternative option.
alternatePaths.linkLabel: EDHREC card page for Arjun, the Shifting Flame

swaps.rationale: Curated creature-for-creature swap: Guttersnipe rewards every instant and sorcery, while Warchief Giant is one of the least theme-aligned creatures in the stock list.
Curated draw/filter swap that trades random discard for proliferate plus reliable card selection.
Curated draw spell swap: the cheaper instant better supports chaining spells and leaves mana available after untapping lands.
Curated sorcery swap from a situational combat effect to a one-mana cantrip that raises the deck's spell density.
Curated instant-for-instant swap: efficient stack interaction protects Mizzix more consistently than a temporary theft effect.
Curated spell-value swap: buyback and copying fit the spellslinger engine better than an expensive token-making sorcery.
Curated graveyard-value swap: flashback turns the graveyard into another spell hand and is more native to Mizzix than a standalone creature.
Curated enchantment-for-enchantment swap that turns the deck's spell volume into copied effects rather than only doubling draw.
Curated mass-removal swap that preserves the X/spell theme while returning a key instant or sorcery from the graveyard.
Curated draw-for-draw swap: delve makes a large draw spell much more efficient in a deck that fills its graveyard with spells.
Curated bounce-for-bounce upgrade: overload provides a scalable reset while remaining an instant Mizzix can discount.
Curated red sweeper swap that keeps the board-control role while offering a lower floor in creature-heavy games.
Curated creature swap: Young Pyromancer converts the deck's many spells into a steady token army instead of relying on combat damage.
Curated ramp swap: a ritual is itself a spell for Mizzix and can create a burst turn rather than waiting for artifact mana.
Curated mana-engine swap that rewards a spell-heavy deck with a large burst for X-spells and copied effects.
Curated instant-for-instant swap from modest burn-plus-selection to deep, graveyard-enabled selection.
Curated cheap-instant swap: both provide flexible early interaction/value, but Impulse more directly finds the next needed spell.
Curated instant-interaction swap that replaces an expensive creature-theft effect with a scalable counterspell and potential X-based damage.
Curated enchantment swap: Summonings rewards the deck's normal casting pattern, while Awaken is reactive and off-plan.
Curated enchantment swap that reduces and scries for the deck's instants and sorceries instead of making temporary attacker tokens.

guides.theme: Simic experience and +1/+1 counters: deploy small creatures to build experience, then repeatedly grow an evasive attacker or a wide creature/token board. The native plan rewards creatures with power 2 or less, counter payoffs, and combat-based evasion.

picks.name: Llanowar Elves
picks.reason: A one-mana creature that accelerates mana while also triggering Ezuri's experience plan; the opened guide specifically recommends it.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was quoted; choose an inexpensive printing if available.

picks.name: Fathom Mage
picks.reason: Turns the deck's +1/+1-counter engine into repeatable card draw and is one of EDHREC's most-supported additions for this precon.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was quoted; verify the current printing before purchase.

picks.name: Hardened Scales
picks.reason: A cheap counter multiplier that improves Ezuri's triggers, evolve creatures, and other native counter effects; the upgrade guide names it directly.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was quoted; use a low-cost printing if available.

picks.name: Herald of Secret Streams
picks.reason: Makes creatures with +1/+1 counters unblockable while remaining a small creature that contributes to Ezuri's experience count; explicitly recommended by the guide and EDHREC.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was quoted; check current listings rather than assuming a price.

picks.name: Inspiring Call
picks.reason: Protects a counter-heavy board and draws cards, directly addressing the precon's vulnerability to removal while preserving its native mechanic.
picks.budgetNote: No source price was quoted; verify the current printing before purchase.

alternatePaths.title: Kaseto counters-and-evasion build

alternatePaths.title: Kruphix big-mana/value path
alternatePaths.description: Use Kruphix, God of Horizons as commander for a more mana-and-card-advantage-oriented Simic build; EDHREC provides a dedicated alternate-commander upgrade page for this exact precon.
alternatePaths.linkLabel: EDHREC Swell the Host upgrades for Kruphix, God of Horizons

swaps.rationale: Curated like-for-unlike upgrade: replace a high-power creature that does not advance Ezuri's experience count with a one-mana creature that ramps and does.
Curated draw upgrade: Fathom Mage turns counters into repeatable cards while the precon's six-mana Ambusher is among EDHREC's common cuts.
Curated curve-and-ramp upgrade: Gyre Sage scales with counters and produces mana; Great Oak Guardian is a high-power, high-cost card the guide flags as not triggering Ezuri.
Curated counter-synergy swap: Vorel doubles the deck's central counters, while Day of the Dragons exiles the creatures carrying them and is specifically criticized by the guide.
Curated native-mechanics swap: add a counter multiplier instead of a mass exile effect that resets the board's accumulated counters.
Curated evasion swap: Herald makes countered creatures unblockable, whereas Noble Quarry's forced-block effect does not protect or efficiently close with the deck's counters.
Curated protection-and-cards swap: Inspiring Call protects the counter board and replaces itself; the guide identifies Mirror Match as expensive and disconnected from the plan.
Curated evasive-threat swap: Champion rewards the deck's growing board by making attacks harder to block, replacing a seven-mana creature that does not trigger Ezuri.
Curated proliferate-and-curve swap: Thrummingbird compounds the native counter plan as a small evasive creature, while EDHREC frequently cuts Thelonite Hermit.

Curated counter payoff swap: Sage of Hours converts the deck's counter production into a powerful combat-adjacent payoff, replacing an off-plan equipment package; both cards are individually supported by EDHREC's add/cut data.
Curated draw-to-board upgrade: Chasm Skulker turns card draw into a growing counter creature and tokens, while retaining the deck's counter-and-wide-board identity.
Curated counter-distribution upgrade: Master Biomancer improves every subsequent creature's entry counters instead of relying on a standalone high-power threat.
Curated theme win-condition swap: Simic Ascendancy directly rewards accumulating +1/+1 counters, replacing a mana-intensive token outlet; both are supported by EDHREC's add/cut rankings.
Curated lower-curve interaction swap: Reclamation Sage supplies immediate artifact/enchantment removal while contributing a small creature to Ezuri's experience plan.
Curated flexible-removal swap: Acidic Slime broadens interaction beyond creatures while remaining a creature-based utility spell; both candidates are individually supported by EDHREC.
Curated efficiency swap: cheap stack interaction protects Ezuri and the tall counter creature more efficiently than the six-mana sorcery; EDHREC supports the add and cut candidates.
Curated early-creature swap: Elvish Mystic accelerates the experience engine from turn one, while Loaming Shaman is a commonly cut card on EDHREC.

Curated ramp-for-low-impact-creature swap: Wood Elves advances mana and supplies an experience-triggering body; Caller of the Claw is in the original list and is a less direct fit for the counter plan.
Curated counter utility swap: Zameck Guildmage converts counters into cards and helps manage counters, more directly serving the deck's central mechanic than Patagia Viper.
Curated protection-for-combat swap: Plaxcaster Frogling uses graft counters to protect key creatures, while Broodbirth Viper is a frequent EDHREC cut.

alternatePaths.description: Keep Zedruu as commander but shift the strategy toward draw payoffs: Approach of the Second Sun, Psychosis Crawler, Niv-Mizzet, the Firemind, The Locust God, and Aetherflux Reservoir are all explicitly used in the EDHREC redesign.

swaps.rationale: Both support giving permanents to opponents; Trader does so more directly and repeatedly.
A political card-draw creature replaces a symmetrical draw spell while adding a repeatable gift interaction.
Keeps the shared-resources politics theme while making the draw effect a negotiable artifact.
Trades temporary creature control for a more on-theme permanent exchange effect.
Replaces a narrow donated aura with a repeatable permanent-exchange engine.
Upgrades a one-shot political deterrent into a durable defensive permanent that can later become a Zedruu gift.
Replaces an unfocused attacker with an explicitly supported gift that supplies opponents tokens for political leverage.
Moves creature-based damage from a one-time removal effect to a signature donated threat.
Improves the deck's core draw engine without giving an opponent the same spell-based draw bargain.
Turns Zedruu's card draw into a direct win-condition pressure instead of a situational life-total reset.
Converts the existing draw theme into a clearly supported alternate win condition.
Replaces an expensive, slow artifact with a draw-and-life-gain payoff explicitly used by the redesign.
Strengthens both halves of Zedruu's trigger—cards and life—instead of a one-shot cantrip.
Adds an extra beginning phase to multiply Zedruu upkeep value rather than an unfocused combat scaling effect.
Replaces a destructive six-mana threat with a draw-scaling token engine that can also be donated innocuously.
Keeps card flow online while turning opponents' draws into a repeatable source of advantage.
Replaces a small selection creature with a supported political draw engine that rewards multiple opponent actions.
Swaps a passive defensive body for a deliberately dangerous gift aimed at token-heavy opponents.
Preserves the donated-permanent politics while making the gift a table-wide attack incentive.
Replaces a maintenance-intensive creature with a supported donated threat that punishes artifact-heavy decks.
Upgrades an expensive counterspell into a spell-and-permanent exchange effect that matches the deck's political identity.
Replaces conditional temporary bounce with an explicitly supported way to redirect a creature to another opponent.
Keeps the creature-exchange effect but makes it a cleaner, repeatable part of the gift-and-trade package.
Combines creature exchange with card draw, better serving both native deck mechanics.
Like-for-like upgrade to a donated removal aura; the article explicitly expands the Journey to Nowhere package with Banishing Light.

guides.coverageNote: Source research is complete for this guide. Recommendations draw on the cited sources; paired add/cut swaps are curated, not source-authored one-to-one pairings.
